assertion_analysis.fails_when: Fixture sanity fails if its initial waiting pointer is absent or already queued; this is setup evidence, not release coverage.
Restoring the base unattended pass leaves the clean pointer; the recorded base control fails exactly here.
Keeping the clean worktree after release makes the filesystem observation fail.
Omitting or falsifying the persisted successful-worktree receipt fails the ledger reread.
Reporting the initially present tree as already absent fails this independent precondition check.
Omitting both section completion and waiter release leaves the persisted waiter awaiting-upstream; the queued state is read independently of the call argument.
Omitting section declaration leaves the plan implementable instead of done.
Deleting or corrupting integrated source content fails the known fixture content check; this protects the primary checkout.
Leaving the retired run eligible makes a second pass return it again.
Rewriting the stored release on the second pass fails the independent before/after disk snapshots; no expected receipt is passed to the release function.
Removing an unsafe tree fails the filesystem check; line 125 additionally fails if the unsafe pointer disappeared.
Restoring the old settled classification makes the unsafe run read settled instead of unreadable.
Dropping the specific dirty/unresolvable cause loses the required classification detail; the expected cause is derived from the deliberate fixture defect, not passed as an expected output.
Suppressing the unsafe obligation or duplicating it makes its filtered count differ from one.
Replacing the obligation reason with generic text loses the deliberate fixture cause.
Retiring or mutating the unmerged pointer fails the disk comparison; no snapshot is passed to production code.
Releasing the unmerged tree fails the filesystem check.
Writing a release outcome for unmerged work fails the ledger absence check.
Bypassing a promotion request or pending journal hits the raising _promoted_row sentinel even before the result assertion, proving ordering; unexpected result rows also fail.
Deleting the existing owner pointer fails the filesystem check.
Releasing the existing owner tree fails the filesystem check.
Ignoring the changed attempt identity releases the run and produces a result instead of an empty list.
Modifying or deleting the newer attempt fails the independent pointer disk snapshot comparison.
Releasing the newer attempt tree fails the filesystem check.

assertion_independence: No added assertion compares a supplied expected value to its own echoed input; preserved snapshots are separately read disk state, and expected cause strings identify deliberately introduced defects. The fixture sanity assertion is not counted as production coverage.
